chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'A time will come upon the people when nothing will remain of the Quran except its outline, and nothing of Islam except its name. They will be named by it, but they are the farthest of people from it. Their mosques will be well-built, but they are ruins from guidance. The jurists of that time are the worst of jurists under the shadow of the sky. From them the strife will emerge, and to them it will return.'
ai.seo_question: What are the signs of the decline of the jurists in the era of the Quran's outline?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of Imam al-Sadiq from Imam Ali and the Prophet, warns of an era of 'formalism' where the Quran remains merely in script and Islam only in name, a concept central to Shia critiques of religious superficiality. It specifically identifies the jurists (fuqaha) of that time as the worst under the sky, linking their spiritual emptiness to the emergence and resolution of major tribulations (fitna). This underscores the Shia emphasis on deep, substantive knowledge over mere ritualistic observance.

en.hubeali: H 14927 – Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nowfaly, from Al-Sakuny, who has narrated the following: Abu Abdullahasws has said that the Amir-ul- Momineenasws said: ‘The Rasool Allahsaww said: ‘There will come upon the people a time when nothing will remain from the Quran except for its image, and nothing from Al-Islam except for its name. They will be named by it (as Muslims) but they would be far from it. Their Masjid will be well built but would be ruins in matters of guidance. The Jurists of that era would be the most evil jurists under the shadow of the sky. The strife (Fitna) would commence from them and end up to them’.
en.sarwar: 480. Al-Husayn Bin Muhammad Al-Ashary, from Mu‘alla Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Muhammad Bin Al-Husayn Bin Yazeed who said:

I heard Al-Ridha (a.s.) at Khurasaan and he (a.s.) was saying: ‘We (a.s.), the People (a.s.) of the Household inherited the forgiveness from the Progeny of Yaqoub (as), and we (a.s.) inherited the appreciation from the Progeny of Dawood (as)’. And I (the narrator) think that there was another statement which was forgotten by Muhammad (the narrator), so I said to him, Perhaps it is that he (a.s.) said: ‘And we (a.s.) inherited the patience from the Progeny of Ayub (as)’. He said, ‘It is befitting’. Ali Bin Asbaat said, ‘But rather, I said that because I had heard Yaqoub Bin Yaqteen narrate from some of his men, ‘When Abu Ja’far Al-Mansour went to Al-Medina in the year in which Muhammad and Ibrahim the sons of Abdullah Bin Al-Hassan were killed, he turned towards his uncle Isa Bin Ali. He said to him, ‘O Abu Al-Abbas! The commander of the faithful (the Caliph) has decided that the trees of Al-Medina be cut down, and its fountains blocked, and it be turned upside down’. He said, ‘O commander of the faithful (Caliph), this here is the son (a.s.) of your uncle Ja’far Bin Muhammad (a.s.), send for him and ask him (a.s.) of his opinion’. He (the narrator) said, ‘So he sent a message which Isa informed him (a.s.) of, and then returned back to him. So he said to him, ‘O commander of the faithful (Caliph), Dawood (as) was Granted appreciation, and Ayyub (as) was in affliction so he (as) was patient, and that Yusuf (as) forgave after being in power. So forgive, for you are from the lineage of those ones (as)’.
